trigger: review of PR #2245 (verifier: 480 of 200,000 decimal literals differ, all D_CLAMP)
observed: the decimal grammar clamps the exponent number at MAX_EXPONENT_NUMBER before it adds the digit counts, in both directions: fraction digits ("0." + 723 zeros + "1e10240" gave 1e300) and integer digits beyond the 19 the re-parse keeps ("1" + 1100 zeros + "e-10240" gave about 1e76; this direction was not in PATTERN_ROUTES); the #2215 contract (results exactly the JDK's) was violated for decimal literals
correction: parseDecFloatLiteral of both templates passes DECLINED_EXPONENT (Integer.MIN_VALUE) as both exponents once |exponent number| reaches MAX_EXPONENT_NUMBER, so the decimal kernels decline and FloatingDecimal decides; every exponent number from 1024 up declines (one comparison after the loop, no new local; an unclamped one lies outside the kernel range anyway unless about 700 digits bring it back)
guard: M3NumberParseDecClampAtomsTest 10/10 (pre-image: 8 of 10 fail); decimal differential 400,000 identical to stock (pre-image: 74,487 lines differ); verifier corpus 480 -> 0; DEC_BYTECODE_METHOD_DELTA PASS
lesson: when an accumulator saturates, every later adjustment must come before the saturation test, or the consumer must decline; a corpus must reach every direction in which a later adjustment can undo the saturation
